hypothesis: If terrestrial mammals cannot cross wide seas, no native non-volant terrestrial mammal lives on islands more than about 300 miles (483 km) from a continent or a large continental island.
pass_criterion: Zero native non-volant terrestrial mammal species in IUCN range data on islands whose minimum distance to a continent or great continental island exceeds 483 km, excluding domesticated animals and human-introduced species.
fail_criterion: At least one native non-volant terrestrial mammal species (not introduced) is confirmed on an island more than 483 km from a continent or great continental island.
interpretation: 'Terrestrial mammal' means non-flying, non-marine mammals. 'Great continental island' means islands such as Borneo, Madagascar or Great Britain. Distance is measured to the nearest continent or great continental island. Native status is taken from the IUCN origin field.

dataset.name: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
dataset.publisher: International Union for Conservation of Nature
dataset.why_it_fits: The mammal assessments have range polygons, a terrestrial system flag, and presence and origin codes (native vs introduced). They are used to list native terrestrial mammals on remote islands.
